summary.zh: 酸辣鲜香的泰国国汤，香茅与柠檬叶的热带交响。
summary.en: Thailand's national soup — a tropical symphony of lemongrass, lime and chili.

ingredients.zh: 鱼露 2 大勺、青柠汁 3 大勺
ingredients.en: 2 tbsp fish sauce, 3 tbsp lime juice

steps.zh: 鲜虾去头去壳留尾，虾头虾壳备用；挑去虾线。
steps.en: Peel and devein the prawns, keeping tails on; reserve heads and shells.

steps.zh: 锅中加 800 毫升水，放入虾头虾壳煮 5 分钟熬出虾汤，捞出虾壳。
steps.en: Simmer heads and shells in 800ml water for 5 minutes to make a quick prawn stock; strain.

steps.zh: 虾汤中加入香茅、柠檬叶、南姜、小米辣，煮 3 分钟出香。
steps.en: Add lemongrass, lime leaves, galangal and chilies; boil 3 minutes until fragrant.

steps.zh: 放入草菇和冬阴功酱煮 2 分钟，再下虾仁煮至变色卷曲。
steps.en: Add mushrooms and tom yum paste for 2 minutes, then the prawns until they curl and turn pink.

steps.zh: 关火，加鱼露和青柠汁调味，酸辣度按口味微调。
steps.en: Turn off the heat, then season with fish sauce and lime juice, adjusting sourness to taste.

steps.zh: 装碗撒香菜，喜欢浓汤版（nam khon）可加 2 大勺淡奶。
steps.en: Garnish with cilantro; for the creamy 'nam khon' style, stir in 2 tbsp evaporated milk.

tips.zh: 青柠汁必须关火后再加，久煮会发苦。
tips.en: Always add lime juice off the heat — boiling turns it bitter.

tips.zh: 香茅、南姜、柠檬叶是「冬阴三宝」，缺一不可。
tips.en: Lemongrass, galangal and lime leaves are the 'holy trinity' — no substitutions.

tips.zh: 用虾头熬汤是鲜味翻倍的秘诀。
tips.en: Simmering the prawn heads doubles the umami.

failChecks.zh: 汤发苦：青柠汁加太早或柠檬叶煮太久，关火后再调味。
failChecks.en: Bitter soup? Lime juice added too early or leaves boiled too long — season off the heat.

failChecks.zh: 只有辣没有香：香料没拍碎或煮的时间不够，香茅要拍扁再下锅。
failChecks.en: Heat without aroma? Bruise the lemongrass and give the herbs time to infuse.

failChecks.zh: 虾肉老：虾仁煮过头，变色卷曲立即关火。
failChecks.en: Rubbery prawns? Overcooked — remove from heat as soon as they curl.

culturalStory.zh: 「冬阴」在泰语中意为「酸辣」，「功」是虾。冬阴功起源于泰国中部湄南河畔，河虾丰饶，渔夫以现捞鲜虾与岸边随手可得的香茅、柠檬叶煮汤，酸辣开胃以解湿热。2024 年，冬阴功被联合国教科文组织列入人类非物质文化遗产代表作名录，成为泰国饮食文化的世界名片。
culturalStory.en: 'Tom yum' means hot-and-sour, 'goong' means prawn. Born on the banks of the Chao Phraya River, fishermen boiled fresh river prawns with lemongrass and lime leaves growing nearby — a sour-spicy antidote to the humid climate. In 2024, Tom Yum Goong was inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list, becoming Thailand's culinary gift to the world.
